column1: # Game profile of SUPER ROBOT WARS Y (Switch, update 1.4.1 = v720896). Plays on the Mac
# Format: see dm/games/README.md; bring-up and measurements in README.md beside this file

# Unity 2022.3.44f1 (IL2CPP) with CRIWARE, SDK 18.3.5, NVN; subsdk0 is the movie module. The shaders are Unity's Shader and ComputeShader objects in the UnityFS bundles under Data/, plus the player's GLSLC outputs in main
# The game asks for present interval 1 and runs at 60 fps. Docked (1920x1080)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 4 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup hands application pool - used memory to StandardAllocator as one address region

# (0.91 GB at alias +0.06 GB, returning to main+0xbe7d60) and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. The SDK-wide node area and region alignment cuts apply (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py MATCH_CUTS, implementation 4 of each).
# The layout of Cult of the Lamb and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse: a 1 GB pool and the 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region).
# With the hardware pool the heap check's alias region reached +4.26 GB within its first seconds
# The game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode(near = 0) (log: "depth mode near=0"), so its vertex shaders use the main0_z entries; the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader and ComputeShader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles. The DLC's bundles are read too; no shader has a DLC as its first source
